offduty.title: Beyond the Code
offduty.subtitle: I believe strong results in tech are built on habits formed outside the screen. Here are some things that shape how I work, learn, and solve problems.

training.title: Discipline through metrics
training.caption: I've been strength training for years, and what interests me most isn't the weight, it's the system. I track loads, volume, and progression with the same mindset I use to monitor production performance: data, cycles, continuous adjustments. I've learned that plateaus aren't failures they're signals to revisit the strategy. That mindset of incremental improvement and tolerance for long processes is something I bring directly into software projects.

cooking._image_placeholder: TODO: add cooking image in the future
cooking.title: Cooking to slow down
cooking.caption: Cooking is my disconnection ritual. A deliberately long moment no screen, no notification where the process matters more than the result. Following a complex recipe, respecting each step's timing, adjusting on the fly: it's the only activity in my day that demands full presence without being urgent. I've learned that those who truly know how to slow down can accelerate with far more consistency when it matters.

reading._image_placeholder: TODO: add reading image in the future
reading.title: Reading as perspective expansion
reading.caption: My shelf mixes Clean Code, System Design Interview, and some other software engineering books. I don't read out of obligation, I read because understanding how other engineers thought and failed accelerates my own growth. Beyond books, I subscribe to technical newsletters delivered straight to my inbox: my way of staying current with the ecosystem without relying on algorithms. What goes into your head determines the quality of what comes out in your code.

games.title: Strategy and decision-making under pressure
games.caption: Games are my simulation environment. What attracts me isn't the entertainment itself it's the constant need to read complex systems, make quick decisions with incomplete information, and adapt strategy when the scenario changes. In cooperative games, that becomes coordination, expectation alignment, and situational leadership. The same skills that show up in code review, sprint planning, and production incident response.
